senses.head: apparel
senses.def: The things that are worn by a person; clothing.
senses.sent: The shop sold winter ____ and nothing else from October to March.

senses.head: appreciate
senses.def: To see the worth or quality of.
senses.sent: It took him years to ____ how much work his grandmother had put in.

senses.head: appreciate
senses.def: To increase in value.
senses.sent: The little house on the corner will ____ faster than anything else on the street.

senses.head: continuous
senses.def: Going on without stopping.
senses.sent: The ____ hum of the freezer was the only sound in the whole shop.

senses.head: dissolve
senses.def: To make or become liquid.
senses.sent: Stir until the sugar begins to ____ and the water goes clear again.

senses.head: dissolve
senses.def: To bring or to come to an end.
senses.sent: Rather than find a new coach, they chose to ____ the team altogether.

senses.head: domesticate
senses.def: To tame; to bring plants or animals under human control.
senses.sent: It takes generations to ____ an animal that has always lived wild.

senses.head: domesticate
senses.def: Brought under human control; tamed or cultivated.
senses.sent: Wheat is a ____ grass, bred over thousands of years to hold on to its seed.

senses.head: emerge
senses.def: To come into view; to appear.
senses.sent: We waited the best part of an hour for the otter to ____ from under the bank.

senses.head: emerge
senses.def: To become known.
senses.sent: Not one name would ____ until somebody thought to check the old register.

senses.head: fiber
senses.def: A thin, threadlike part of animal hair or plant tissue; also, an artificial thread that resembles this.
senses.sent: Wool is spun from a ____ that curls naturally, which is why it holds together.

senses.head: fiber
senses.def: An arrangement of body cells that forms muscles and nerves.
senses.sent: Under the microscope you can see every muscle ____ running the same way.

senses.head: fiber
senses.def: A food substance that provides bulk but is not digested.
senses.sent: Skins and stalks are mostly ____, which is why they fill you up so fast.

senses.head: function
senses.def: To serve a purpose.
senses.sent: The bench will ____ as a table if you lay a board across it.

senses.head: function
senses.def: The special purpose something is used for.
senses.sent: The one ____ of that little key is to open the meter cupboard.

senses.head: function
senses.def: An important ceremony or gathering.
senses.sent: There was a ____ at the town hall for the mayor’s fiftieth year in office.

senses.head: hatch
senses.def: To come or to bring forth from an egg.
senses.sent: The eggs should ____ about three weeks after they are laid.

senses.head: hatch
senses.def: To think up.
senses.sent: The two of them would ____ a new plan every time the last one fell through.

senses.head: hatch
senses.def: A small opening with a door or cover.
senses.sent: There is a ____ in the ceiling that lets you up into the loft.

senses.head: inhibit
senses.def: To prevent from doing something or to prevent from happening.
senses.sent: Cold weather will ____ the yeast, and the dough will never rise.

senses.head: inhibit
senses.def: Held back because of shyness.
senses.sent: He was too ____ to put his hand up even when he knew the answer.

senses.head: minute
senses.def: Very small; tiny.
senses.sent: The crack was so ____ that you needed a magnifying glass to find it.

senses.head: motion
senses.def: Movement.
senses.sent: The gentle ____ of the train put half the carriage to sleep.

senses.head: motion
senses.def: A suggestion on which members at a meeting must vote.
senses.sent: Somebody put forward a ____ to move the meeting to Thursday, and it passed.

senses.head: motion
senses.def: To signal.
senses.sent: The guard would ____ us through without ever looking up.

senses.head: motion
senses.def: Not moving; stationary.
senses.sent: The heron stood ____ in the shallows and did not blink once.

senses.head: sheathe
senses.def: To cover with something that protects.
senses.sent: Builders ____ the whole frame in plastic sheeting before the rain comes.

senses.head: shed
senses.def: To lose; to give up.
senses.sent: Our dog will ____ so much hair in June that we brush him out in the yard.

senses.head: shed
senses.def: To cause to flow.
senses.sent: She did not ____ a single tear until the dog came back.

senses.head: shed
senses.def: To throw off water without letting it soak through.
senses.sent: A good waxed coat will ____ rain for hours on end.

senses.head: shed
senses.def: To send out or give off.
senses.sent: A full moon can ____ enough light to walk home by.

senses.head: transfer
senses.def: To move, carry, send, or change from one person or place to another.
senses.sent: The nurse had to ____ him to a bigger hospital the same evening.

senses.head: transfer
senses.def: The act of transferring.
senses.sent: The ____ of the trophy from one school to the other was done at assembly.

senses.head: transfer
senses.def: A ticket used for transferring from one bus or train to another.
senses.sent: Ask the driver for a ____ and the second bus will not cost you anything.

rounds.name: Worn, woven, eaten
rounds.blurb: Clothing, a covering, and the one word here that means three quite different threads.

rounds.name: Coming out and moving about
rounds.blurb: Nine meanings across four words. Watch hatch and motion — each of them changes its job partway down.

rounds.name: Going, giving off, coming apart
rounds.blurb: Shed alone does four jobs. Read all nine of these together and the pattern is easier than the list looks.

rounds.name: Held back, or let loose
rounds.blurb: Two roots with a second form each, plus a word for never stopping and a word for very small indeed.

rounds.name: What a thing is worth, and what it is for
rounds.blurb: Two words, five meanings, and no overlap between them at all.
